title: Armored Core: Master of Arena
subtitle: Climb the rankings to reach one pilot

body: Armored Core: Master of Arena is FromSoftware's third PlayStation mecha combat game, first released in Japan on 4 February 1999. A survivor joins the Raven's Nest to confront Hustler One, the pilot blamed for the battle that killed their family. The journey gives the Arena a central place, turning a sequence of ranked opponents into the route towards a personal objective. Missions and machine customisation remain part of the campaign, but the next rival supplies a clear reason to return to the garage and improve the build.

The Arena concentrates combat on the capabilities of another Armored Core. Equipment, movement and weapon choice have to work against a rival who can exploit the player's weaknesses. Save data from either earlier PlayStation game can be imported, preserving a machine and parts already earned. That continuity gives experienced players a head start without removing the need to adapt. A new opponent can expose a familiar build's limitations, turning the ranking ladder into a series of practical questions about how the machine should be changed.

Ranker MK allows custom opponents to be created and then fought in the Arena, giving the workshop another purpose beyond the player's own machine. The feature extends the pleasure of assembly into the opposition itself: a design can become something to test against. Music by Kota Hoshino, Tsukasa Saitoh and Keiichiro Segawa accompanies the final release of the original PlayStation trilogy. North America received the game in 2000, while Europe missed an original release. Armored Core 2 then carried the series' garage and mercenary career onto PlayStation 2.
